summary: All example simulations pass, and none of the 5 open questions is blocking. The package is still not ready for four reasons. Decision D-036 has new evidence and must be re-confirmed (the check report lists this as an error). The written H-child rule and the decision table give different answers. The Liechtenstein status is inconsistent and its question order is unclear. Four technical or unsourced behaviours have leaked into the stories. Fix these and the package should reach ready_with_caveats. The caveats would be the open questions for the pension fund and D-009: before go-live, a domain expert compares Lonio's tariff codes with the calculator.

findings.title: D-036 has new evidence and needs re-confirming
findings.why: The decision on the emailed copy was made before Anna's email arrived. The email says the copy holds only the submitted answers, exactly as submitted, with no derived values. Until D-036 is re-confirmed, US-08.4 rests on an outdated decision.
findings.action: Check D-036 against the email, then confirm, update or drop it, and run `pipeline reconfirm D-036`. Resolve this together with finding 6.

findings.title: H-child rule text contradicts the decision table
findings.why: The written rule says an H child must live in the employee's household. Row 21 and AC-06.3.3 count a child outside the household as an H child (H1N). This changes the tariff letter (H/P vs A/L), so the computed code would be wrong in one of the two readings.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement major (feature.md H rule vs row 21 / AC-06.3.3); trace_judge rule.single_parent_h_tariff, item.has_children, item.child_main_financial_contributor
findings.action: Add a decision to decisions.yaml saying which is right. The calculator run in F-c2faa7 supports the table. Then align the rule text and cite the facts behind it (c78e0c, 562299, 97139a).

findings.title: Liechtenstein residents: status and question order undefined
findings.why: The US-01.3 example records 'subject to source tax: yes' with no source tax questions. D-007 instead asks the questions and can give 'in principle no liability'. Denomination, spouse and children answers are asked before the cross-border questions but are not needed for these employees, which goes against data minimisation (G-01).
findings.evidence: trace_judge story.US-01.3; dev_refinement major (feature.md steps 6/6a vs 7); info US-01.3, US-05.7 (>45 days double-taxation-agreement flag)
findings.action: Decide what is recorded as 'subject to source tax' for Liechtenstein residents (yes, no, or a separate status). Decide whether the Liechtenstein questions come first and the later ones are skipped. Decide whether the >45-days case is flagged for HR.

findings.title: US-05.7 adds 'cannot be computed yet' behaviour that no source asked for
findings.why: The spec chooses one fallback for unexplored child combinations, but OQ-child-paths-undetermined still lists 'HR determines the code' as an option. Engineering would build an outcome nobody has agreed to.
findings.evidence: tech_leak US-05.7; trace_judge story.US-05.6 (AC-05.6.4), story.US-05.7 (AC-05.7.5), rule.source_tax_result
findings.action: Pick the interim behaviour for OQ-child-paths-undetermined in decisions.yaml and cite it in AC-05.6.4 and AC-05.7.5, or remove the behaviour from the stories.

findings.title: US-08.3 widens 'no history kept' to every derived value
findings.why: This is a data-retention decision. D-033 covers only the first working day. The story also cites a 'Julia changed start date' incident that no source backs.
findings.action: Either narrow the wording to what D-033 says, or add a decision that covers all derived results. Remove the unbacked incident or cite a source for it.

findings.title: Emailed copy: retention of the email address and scope of 'answers' unclear
findings.why: Nothing says whether the email address typed in for the copy is stored or shown to HR. Nothing says whether the 'send me a copy' answer and the address count as answers that appear in the copy. AC-08.4.3 lists excluded derived values that no source names.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement major US-08.4; trace_judge rule.employee_copy_content, story.US-08.4; inferred item.copy_email_address
findings.action: While re-confirming D-036, decide how long the address is kept and what exactly the copy contains. Write AC-08.4.3 as 'no derived values' rather than an unsourced list.

findings.title: No date checks for the first working day or dates of birth
findings.why: A wrong first working day leads straight to a wrong insurance start date for the pension fund. Engineering cannot write validation without rules.
findings.action: Ask HR and decide: can the first working day be in the past, and how far ahead can it be? Are there age limits for the employee's date of birth, and any check on the spouse's date of birth?

findings.title: Implementation and UI wording in the business rules
findings.why: The text refers to 'the expression', and US-06.1 describes add/remove child controls. These are design and implementation choices, not requirements.
findings.evidence: tech_leak feature.md ('The expression evaluates one child…'); tech_leak US-06.1
findings.action: Rewrite as business rules: 'each child is assessed separately; the counted children are added up' and 'answers are collected for each child'. Leave the UI to design.

findings.title: Some rule rows cite facts that are not in their cited set
findings.why: Several rows (for example 'other country → base tariff' and 'not subject → no result') rest on facts the rule does not cite. That breaks the link from rule to source.
findings.evidence: trace_judge rule.source_tax_residence, rule.cross_border_tariff_applies, rule.liechtenstein_no_source_tax_in_principle, rule.source_tax_result (F-52b67a, 332e2a, b6d9b3, 2eab9a not cited); item.daily_return_germany, item.child_parental_custody; story.US-04.1 (F-b84498)
findings.action: Add the missing fact citations, or mark these rows as inferred and confirm them.

findings.title: Example tables and question wording need cleanup before they can serve as tests
findings.why: The example tables mix '–', 'asked' and 'required'. The certificate question is phrased both as 'has' and 'have provided', and the two readings give different tariffs. 'Calendar year' is not defined for employees who start late in the year. The permit reminder text has no owner.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement info US-01.2, US-03.3, US-07.2 (×2), US-08.1, US-06.1 (more than 9 children), US-06.2 (stepchildren)
findings.action: Correct the example tables. Decide whether the certificate question means 'has' or 'has provided', and which year is meant. Name who writes the permit reminder text and by when. Set a maximum number of children and how a code is formed above 9. Decide how the questions apply to stepchildren.
